content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To give coats to the homeless, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Design a promotional flyer (2 hours)
Step 2. Load the final inventory into the delivery van (45 minutes)
Step 3. Create a digital map of distribution points (1 hour)
Step 4. Finalize the list of volunteers for the event day (30 minutes)
Step 5. Set up a physical donation drop-box at the library (1 hour)
Step 6. Print labels for sorted coat sizes (20 minutes)
Step 7. Confirm the date with the local shelter (15 minutes)
Step 8. Draft the initial project proposal (3 hours)
Step 9. Research high-need areas in the city (4 hours)
Step 10. Recruit a volunteer coordinator (2 hours)
Step 11. Purchase heavy-duty storage bins (1 hour)
Step 12. Secure a temporary storage unit (2 days)
Step 13. Create a social media account for the drive (30 minutes)
Step 14. Reach out to local dry cleaners for cleaning sponsorships (3 days)
Step 15. Apply for a city solicitation permit (1 week)
Step 16. Launch the online donation portal (4 hours)
Step 17. Purchase folding tables for the distribution site (1 hour)
Step 18. Organize a team meeting to discuss logistics (90 minutes)
Step 19. Record a video appeal for donations (1 hour)
Step 20. Contact local businesses for corporate sponsorships (5 days)
Step 21. Hire a truck driver for the distribution day (2 hours)
Step 22. Conduct a final safety briefing for all staff (1 hour)
Step 23. Buy refreshments for the volunteers (45 minutes)
Step 24. Inspect the quality of donated coats (4 hours)
Step 25. Sort coats by gender and age group (3 hours)
Step 26. Identify key community partners (1 day)
Step 27. Set up a dedicated email address for inquiries (20 minutes)
Step 28. Rent a portable heater for the outdoor site (2 hours)
Step 29. Arrange for a secondary backup storage space (1 day)
Step 30. Purchase packing tape and markers (30 minutes)
Step 31. Distribute flyers to local cafes (3 hours)
Step 32. Order custom "Volunteer" t-shirts (5 days)
Step 33. Post the flyer on community bulletin boards (2 hours)
Step 34. Draft a press release for local news (2 hours)
Step 35. Establish a system for tracking inventory (4 hours)
Step 36. Label all bins with size and type (2 hours)
Step 37. Design a "Thank You" card for donors (1 hour)
Step 38. Solicit donations of hangers and racks (2 days)
Step 39. Contact a photographer to document the event (1 hour)
Step 40. Secure a permit for the distribution park (2 weeks)
Step 41. Create a budget spreadsheet (3 hours)
Step 42. Partner with a local laundry service (4 days)
Step 43. Recruit a team of 10 sorting volunteers (3 hours)
Step 44. Print "Coat Distribution Today" banners (2 hours)
Step 45. Set up a coat repair station for minor tears (4 hours)
Step 46. Source wholesale winter gloves and hats (3 days)
Step 47. Bag the sorted coats for easy transport (5 hours)
Step 48. Gather cardboard boxes from local shops (2 hours)
Step 49. Inventory the donated hats and gloves (2 hours)
Step 50. Size-tag every individual coat (6 hours)
Step 51. Pack the distribution kits (3 hours)
Step 52. Arrange the furniture at the distribution site (2 hours)
Step 53. Sanitize the sorting area (1 hour)
Step 54. Write a volunteer training manual (4 hours)
Step 55. Request a police presence for crowd control (1 week)
Step 56. Move the bins from storage to the staging area (3 hours)
Step 57. Set up the check-in desk at the event (1 hour)
Step 58. Rent a PA system for announcements (3 hours)
Step 59. Post a "Call for Volunteers" on social media (30 minutes)
Step 60. Conduct a site walkthrough (2 hours)
Step 61. Open a bank account for cash donations (2 hours)
Step 62. Load the tables and heaters into the truck (1 hour)
Step 63. Research weather forecasts for the event week (30 minutes)
Step 64. Coordinate with a local soup kitchen to provide food (4 days)
Step 65. Verify the driver's commercial license (30 minutes)
Step 66. Organize a "mending circle" for button repairs (3 hours)
Step 67. Draft a liability waiver for volunteers (2 hours)
Step 68. Interview a local meteorologist for timing advice (1 hour)
Step 69. Hand out information cards to the homeless (4 hours)
Step 70. Source a mobile phone for the event day (1 hour)
Step 71. Buy plastic garment bags (1 hour)
Step 72. Launch a radio ad campaign (3 days)
Step 73. Secure a fuel card for the delivery truck (1 hour)
Step 74. Buy a heavy-duty stapler and staples (15 minutes)
Step 75. Assign roles to the core leadership team (2 hours)
Step 76. Purchase a first-aid kit (30 minutes)
Step 77. Call the park department for gate access (20 minutes)
Step 78. Send a confirmation email to all volunteers (1 hour)
Step 79. Buy heavy-duty trash bags for cleanup (30 minutes)
Step 80. Create a sign-up sheet for the donation bins (30 minutes)
Step 81. Set up the outdoor coat racks (2 hours)
Step 82. Arrange for a waste removal service (2 hours)
Step 83. Print directional signage for the park (1 hour)
Step 84. Purchase bottled water for the crew (1 hour)
Step 85. Check the park for electrical outlets (1 hour)
Step 86. Organize the distribution flow path (2 hours)
Step 87. Write a script for the event greeters (1 hour)
Step 88. Hire a professional cleaner for the final venue (4 hours)
Step 89. Rent a van for the volunteer carpool (3 hours)
Step 90. Finalize the coat distribution counts (1 hour)
